# TORCS and the SCR Protocol

**TORCS** is an open-source racing simulator. **SCR** (Simulated Car Racing) is the competition
patch that exposes a driving agent over a **UDP socket** instead of requiring it to be compiled into
the simulator as a C++ robot. Everything the PPO agent in
[[it-applications-in-business-and-commerce]] can see or do passes through that socket, and the
protocol's shape determines the whole design of the project.

## The sensor and actuator surface

The client (`snakeoil3_gym.py`, 605 lines, vendored from Chris X Edwards' original snakeoil library
and present identically in both agent trees) encodes and decodes a string-based sensor/actuator
message over a blocking `recvfrom` with a timeout.

**Readable:** `angle`, `curLapTime`, `damage`, `distFromStart`, `distRaced`, `focus`, `fuel`,
`gear`, `lastLapTime`, `opponents`, `racePos`, `rpm`, `speedX`, `speedY`, `speedZ`, `track`,
`trackPos`, `wheelSpinVel`, `z`.

**Writable:** `accel`, `brake`, `clutch`, `gear`, `steer`, `focus`, `meta`.

That list is the entire observable universe. The 33-dimensional tracking-error state in
[[residual-reinforcement-learning]] is a function of it; the reward terms catalogued in
[[reward-shaping]] are functions of it; and every "why doesn't the agent just…" question about this
project usually has the answer *because the protocol does not expose it*.

## The constraint that shaped the architecture

The clearest example: the racing line in [[minimum-curvature-racing-line]] needs track geometry, and
TORCS holds that geometry in a C++ runtime structure the socket cannot reach.

> "`tTrackSeg` is a TORCS C++ runtime structure. It is ONLY visible to a robot compiled inside
> TORCS. Our agent talks to TORCS over the SCR UDP protocol (snakeoil3_gym.py) and CANNOT see
> tTrackSeg."
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/code/a.bhuiyan/guide.txt, 2026-07-10

The response was to obtain the same geometry offline from the track XML — recorded as
[[parse-track-xml-not-ttrackseg]]. Runtime localisation then uses only sensors that *are* available:
`distFromStart` for arc length, `trackPos` for lateral offset, `angle` for heading error, `speedX`
for speed.

Two further protocol consequences show up in the code: gear must be *commanded*, so a gearbox
policy had to be built (see [[data-driven-gearing-over-hand-tuned-rpm-bands]]); and the only
acceleration signal available is the difference of successive `speedX` readings, which the
`gear_strategy_max_jerk` branch report explicitly calls out as noisy.

## Deliberately not vendored

The simulator itself — roughly 1 GB of third-party C/C++ per branch — is excluded, and the
`.gitignore` says why rather than silently dropping it:

> "# Vendored TORCS simulator — a third-party prerequisite, not committed here"
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/.gitignore, 2026-07-10

`NOTICE` attributes TORCS, SCR and the upstream `gym_torcs` wrapper. `project/README.md` carries a
"Not included:" callout naming exactly what is and is not the team's work. Good
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]], and the reason nothing in this repo runs without a manual
TORCS install first.
